about.emergency: Chest pain, feeling unwell, serious difficulty breathing: call 112 straight away.
about.helpNote: Your doctor, your pharmacist or a stop-smoking specialist can also support you, including with stop-smoking treatments.
about.helpSubtitle: Free helplines are available. Getting support is a strength, not a failure.

limits.coach: The coach runs on local rules, not on a connected AI.
limits.community: Family mode, shared challenges and the forum need a server: they are not available yet.
limits.notifications: Notifications depend on your phone's system and may be delayed.
limits.offline: Everything works offline: nothing is backed up to the cloud. Remember to export your data.
limits.widget: The home screen widget needs a compiled build of the app: it is not included in this version.

about.notMedical: Souffle is a behavioural support tool. It is not a medical device and does not replace advice from a health professional.
about.title: About
about.what: Souffle helps you get through cravings with short actions, home workouts and progress tracking. Health estimates are general guides, never measurements.

prompts.coffee: I want to smoke after my coffee

anger.message: Release the tension with the anti-anger workout: a few minutes is enough.
anger.why: Moving helps reduce the physical tension that comes with anger.

anger_gentle.message: Breathe first, slowly. The anger will ease.
anger_gentle.why: You mentioned some limitations: calm breathing suits you better than intense effort.

boredom.message: Keep your mind busy with a little game, or move for a few minutes.
boredom.why: Boredom leaves room for cravings. A short, absorbing activity helps you get past it.

craving_coffee.message: Change the ritual: drink your coffee somewhere else, then do the short anti-coffee routine.
craving_coffee.why: Coffee and cigarettes often go together. Changing place and keeping your hands busy helps break that link.

craving_general.message: Start with 2 minutes of guided breathing.
craving_general.why: A craving rises and then falls. Breathing helps you get through the moment.

missed_sessions.message: That's OK. Pick up again with a short workout, at your own pace.
missed_sessions.why: Consistency builds over time, not by catching up all at once.

motivation.message: Reread your pact: your reasons are still there.
motivation.why: Motivation goes up and down, that's normal. Coming back to your why helps you stay on course.

no_sport.message: No problem. A reset workout of a few minutes is enough to restart the week.
no_sport.why: Getting back into it with a short workout is easier than a big one.

pain.message: Look after yourself first: no exercise right now.
pain.why: Pain, dizziness or feeling unwell are signals to respect. Exercise can wait until you feel better.

proud.message: Well done! Keep a record of this win in your journal.
proud.why: Rereading your successes really helps in harder moments.

relapsed.message: One cigarette doesn't erase your journey. Let's log it together, no judgement.
relapsed.why: Noting what happened helps you prepare for next time. Your XP, badges and past savings are yours to keep.

sleep.message: Note your night in your journal and choose a wind-down workout this evening.
sleep.why: Sleep and cravings are often linked. Noting them helps you spot your own patterns.

stress.message: Two minutes of guided breathing to ease the pressure.
stress.why: Breathing out for longer than you breathe in helps your body calm down.

tired.message: A gentle mobility workout, or simply rest.
tired.why: Tiredness makes cravings stronger. Listen to your body: recovery is part of the programme too.

unknown.message: I'm not sure I understood. Which of these situations is closest to yours?
unknown.why: I only recognise a few specific situations: choose one below.

coach.subtitle: Practical tips for your situation.
coach.title: Coach

arm_circles.easier: Make smaller circles, elbows slightly bent.
arm_circles.instructions: Arms out to the sides, make small circles forwards, then backwards.
arm_circles.name: Arm circles
arm_circles.safety: Stop if you feel pain in your shoulder.

box_breathing_soft.easier: Drop the pauses and breathe continuously.
box_breathing_soft.instructions: Breathe in for 4 seconds, pause briefly if it feels comfortable, breathe out for 4 seconds, then a short pause.
box_breathing_soft.name: Gentle box breathing
box_breathing_soft.safety: At the slightest discomfort, go back to natural breathing.

calf_raise.easier: Keep your hands on the back of a chair.
calf_raise.harder: Do it on one leg, holding on.
calf_raise.instructions: Slowly rise up onto your toes, then lower back down.
calf_raise.name: Calf raises

cat_cow.harder: Slow down and lengthen each breath.
cat_cow.instructions: On all fours, round your back as you breathe out, then gently arch it as you breathe in.
cat_cow.name: Cat-cow
cat_cow.safety: Move slowly, without straining your lower back.

chair_squat.easier: Use your hands on your thighs or on the armrests.
chair_squat.harder: Just touch the seat lightly without sitting down.
chair_squat.instructions: Feet hip-width apart, sit down slowly on the chair, then stand up by pushing through your heels.
chair_squat.name: Chair squat
chair_squat.safety: Knees in line with your feet, stable chair placed against a wall.

child_pose.easier: Slide a cushion under your bottom or your forehead.
child_pose.harder: Widen your knees for a deeper stretch.
child_pose.instructions: Kneeling, sit back on your heels and stretch your arms out in front of you, forehead towards the floor.
child_pose.name: Child's pose
child_pose.safety: Avoid this pose if your knees are painful.

dead_bug.easier: Only move your legs, one at a time.
dead_bug.harder: Extend your arm and leg further, more slowly.
dead_bug.instructions: On your back, arms towards the ceiling, knees bent at 90°. Slowly extend one arm and the opposite leg, then switch.
dead_bug.name: Dead bug
dead_bug.safety: Keep your lower back in contact with the floor.

glute_bridge.harder: Hold for 3 seconds at the top of the movement.
glute_bridge.instructions: On your back, knees bent, lift your hips by squeezing your glutes, then lower slowly.
glute_bridge.name: Glute bridge

hamstring_stretch.harder: Gently bring your chest closer to your leg.
hamstring_stretch.instructions: One leg straight out in front of you, heel on the floor, lean your upper body forward with a straight back. Switch sides.
hamstring_stretch.name: Hamstring stretch

high_knees.easier: March on the spot lifting your knees, without hopping.
high_knees.instructions: Drive your knees up dynamically while swinging your arms.
high_knees.name: High knees
high_knees.safety: Land softly, on the balls of your feet.

hip_stretch.easier: Hold the position without leaning forward.
hip_stretch.harder: Lean a little further, back straight.
hip_stretch.instructions: Sitting on a chair, rest one ankle on the opposite knee and lean forward slightly. Switch sides.
hip_stretch.name: Hip stretch

incline_pushup.easier: Use a higher surface, or the wall.
incline_pushup.harder: Use a lower surface, like a chair against a wall.
incline_pushup.instructions: Hands on a table or a stable surface, body in a straight line. Lower your chest towards the edge, then push back up.
incline_pushup.name: Incline push-ups
incline_pushup.safety: Make sure the surface cannot slide.

jumping_jacks.easier: No-jump version: step one leg out at a time while raising your arms.
jumping_jacks.instructions: Jump while spreading your arms and legs, then come back with feet together.
jumping_jacks.name: Jumping jacks
jumping_jacks.safety: Land softly. Switch to the no-jump version at the slightest discomfort.

lunge.easier: Hold the back of a chair and reduce the range of movement.
lunge.harder: Do a reverse lunge, more slowly.
lunge.instructions: Take a big step forward, lower down by bending both knees, then come back. Alternate legs.
lunge.name: Adapted lunges
lunge.safety: Keep your front knee above your ankle.

march.easier: Stay close to a wall and simply lift your heels.
march.harder: Lift your knees higher and speed up slightly.
march.instructions: Lift your knees to a comfortable height while swinging your arms, back straight, breathing steadily.
march.name: Marching on the spot
march.safety: Keep a pace where you can still talk.

mountain_climber_slow.easier: Hands on a chair wedged against a wall.
mountain_climber_slow.harder: Increase the pace while keeping your back straight.
mountain_climber_slow.instructions: Supporting yourself on your hands, slowly bring one knee towards your chest, then the other.
mountain_climber_slow.name: Slow mountain climbers
mountain_climber_slow.safety: Wrists under your shoulders, hips steady.

neck_rolls.harder: Hold each position for one slow breath.
neck_rolls.instructions: Gently tilt your head towards one shoulder, then the other. Then look right and left, without forcing.
neck_rolls.name: Neck mobility
neck_rolls.safety: Avoid full, fast rotations of your head.

plank_knees.harder: Move onto your feet if it feels comfortable.
plank_knees.instructions: Resting on your forearms and knees, line up your head, back and hips. Breathe calmly.
plank_knees.name: Plank on knees
plank_knees.safety: Don't hold your breath. Stop if your lower back pulls.

recovery_breathing.easier: Simply breathe at your own pace.
recovery_breathing.harder: Lengthen the breath out a little, without forcing.
recovery_breathing.instructions: Breathe in gently through your nose, breathe out for longer through your mouth, shoulders relaxed.
recovery_breathing.name: Recovery breathing

seated_forward_fold.easier: Keep your hands resting on your thighs.
seated_forward_fold.harder: Let your hands move down towards the floor.
seated_forward_fold.instructions: Sitting on the edge of a chair, slowly lean your upper body towards your thighs, arms relaxed.
seated_forward_fold.name: Seated forward fold
seated_forward_fold.safety: Come back up slowly to avoid feeling dizzy.

seated_leg_extension.harder: Keep your leg straight for 5 seconds.
seated_leg_extension.instructions: Sit on the edge of a chair, straighten one leg in front of you, hold for 2 seconds, lower it, then switch legs.
seated_leg_extension.name: Seated leg extension
seated_leg_extension.safety: Keep your back straight, without leaning back.

seated_twist.instructions: Sitting on a chair, gently turn your upper body to the right using the chair back for support, then to the left.
seated_twist.name: Seated twist
seated_twist.safety: Sit up tall before you twist, without forcing.

shadow_boxing.harder: Add a small side step between sets.
shadow_boxing.instructions: Feet apart, throw loose punches into the air, alternating arms.
shadow_boxing.name: Shadow boxing

shoulder_mobility.instructions: Roll your shoulders backwards, then forwards, relaxing your neck.
shoulder_mobility.name: Shoulder mobility
shoulder_mobility.safety: Stay within a comfortable range of movement.

side_plank_knees.easier: Lift your hips for just a few seconds, then lower them.
side_plank_knees.harder: Straighten your legs, resting on your feet.
side_plank_knees.instructions: Lie on your side, resting on your forearm, knees bent. Lift your hips. Switch sides halfway through.
side_plank_knees.name: Adapted side plank
side_plank_knees.safety: Keep your elbow right under your shoulder.

squat.easier: Don't go as low, or do a chair squat.
squat.instructions: Feet apart, lower down as if sitting, weight in your heels, then come back up as you breathe out.
squat.name: Squat
squat.safety: Knees in line with your feet, back straight.

standing_balance.easier: Keep one hand on the chair.
standing_balance.harder: Let go of the chair for a few seconds, always within reach.
standing_balance.instructions: Next to a chair, lift one foot off the floor and hold your balance, then switch feet.
standing_balance.name: Standing balance
standing_balance.safety: Always stay close to something stable.

step_jacks.easier: Only raise your arms to shoulder height.
step_jacks.harder: Speed up while staying in control.
step_jacks.instructions: Step one leg out to the side while raising your arms, come back, then alternate.
step_jacks.name: Step jacks (no jump)

wall_pushup.easier: Bring your feet closer to the wall.
wall_pushup.harder: Move your feet further from the wall.
wall_pushup.instructions: Hands on the wall at shoulder height, feet a little way back. Bend your elbows to bring your chest towards the wall, then push back.
wall_pushup.name: Wall push-ups
wall_pushup.safety: Keep your body in a straight line, without arching your back.

c1d.description: Between day 1 and day 3, withdrawal signs often show up: irritability, nervousness, disturbed sleep, less appetite. It's common, temporary, and it means your body is readjusting.
c1d.title: Withdrawal may show up

c1m.description: Many people describe a clearer head, better focus and more energy. The loss of motivation linked to regular use is reversible once you stop.
c1m.title: A clearer head

c1w.description: For many people, the worst of the withdrawal is behind them after the first week.
c1w.title: The peak has passed

c2d.description: Withdrawal is usually strongest between day 2 and day 6. Hang in there: it's the hardest stretch, and it doesn't last.
c2d.title: The toughest days

c2w.description: Most withdrawal signs last 4 to 14 days. For most people they ease off clearly.
c2w.title: Withdrawal fades

c3m.description: Cannabis disrupts sleep cycles. Sleep problems are often the most stubborn, sometimes for several months, then they ease. If they persist, talk to a doctor.
c3m.title: Sleep recovers

c3w.description: Withdrawal syndrome usually lasts up to 3 weeks. Sleep and strange dreams can take longer to get back to normal.
c3w.title: Withdrawal ends

m1m.description: Between 1 and 9 months, coughing and shortness of breath decrease.
m1m.title: Cough and breathlessness

m1y.description: After one year, your risk of coronary heart disease is about half that of a person who smokes.
m1y.title: Heart

m20min.description: Your heart rate and blood pressure start to drop.
m20min.title: Heart and blood pressure

m24h.description: Carbon monoxide has been flushed out and your lungs start to clear.
m24h.title: Carbon monoxide gone

m2w.description: Between 2 and 12 weeks, your circulation improves and your lung function increases.
m2w.title: Circulation

m3m.description: Between 3 and 9 months, coughing, sinus congestion, tiredness and shortness of breath decrease. Chest infections become less likely.
m3m.title: Airways

m48h.description: There is no nicotine left in your body. Your senses of taste and smell start to improve.
m48h.title: Taste and smell

m72h.description: Breathing often becomes easier and your energy comes back.
m72h.title: Easier breathing

m8h.description: The levels of carbon monoxide and nicotine in your blood have roughly halved.
m8h.title: Less carbon monoxide

cudit.disclaimer: This is a screening test, not a diagnosis. CUDIT-R questions (Adamson et al., 2010), official English wording.

interpretation.hazardous: Your score (8 or more) points to hazardous use. Cutting down or quitting can really make a difference, and you don't have to do it alone.
interpretation.low: Your score is below the screening threshold (8). That doesn't mean your use is risk-free: if you want to cut down or quit, Souffle is here to help.
interpretation.possible_disorder: Your score (12 or more) points to a possible cannabis use disorder. Talking to a doctor or a specialist service can really help; you'll find contacts in "Find help".

q1.question: How often do you use cannabis?

q2.question: How many hours were you "stoned" on a typical day when you had been using cannabis?

q3.question: How often during the past 6 months did you find that you were not able to stop using cannabis once you had started?

q4.question: How often during the past 6 months did you fail to do what was normally expected from you because of using cannabis?

q5.question: How often in the past 6 months have you devoted a great deal of your time to getting, using, or recovering from cannabis?

q6.question: How often in the past 6 months have you had a problem with your memory or concentration after using cannabis?

q7.question: How often do you use cannabis in situations that could be physically hazardous, such as driving, operating machinery, or caring for children?

q8.a1: Yes, but not in the past 6 months

interpretation.very_low: Your physical dependence seems very low. Habits and situations still matter: Souffle helps you spot them.
